title: Water heater: stored water and the magnesium anode
summary: A tank water heater holds roughly 70 to 450 litres of clean water, depending on size (Bradford White electric), and a magnesium anode rod you can shave into fire starter. Electric ones also give heating elements and thermostats; gas ones already disconnected from their gas pipe give a gas control valve, thermocouple and igniter. Cut the power or gas, close the inlet, and let hot water cool before draining.

steps.text: Shut off the energy. Electric: switch off its breaker, even if the grid is down, so the elements can't fire in an empty tank if power returns (Alberta emergency water, Bradford White electric). Gas: turn the gas control knob to OFF and close the gas valve on the pipe.
steps.warn: Electric heaters often run on 240 V. Prove it dead with a meter before touching any wiring.

steps.text: Close the cold water inlet valve on the top of the tank. This stops dirty mains water flowing in and keeps the stored water clean.
Feel the tank. If it is warm, wait: an insulated tank holds its heat for a long time, and water at 60 °C (140 °F) can scald in under 5 seconds (Bradford White electric).
steps.warn: Water from the tank can scald. Let it cool, or drain slowly into a metal container with gloves on.

steps.text: Let air in at the top: open a hot tap in the building, or lift the lever on the pressure relief valve near the top. Without air coming in, water won't flow out: Bradford White and A.O. Smith both have you open a hot tap to drain the tank (Bradford White electric, A.O. Smith gas, Alberta emergency water). Lifting the relief valve's lever releases hot water under pressure (Bradford White electric), so do it only once the tank is cool, and keep clear of the outlet. If the hot water hasn't been used for two weeks or more, extremely flammable hydrogen can collect in the system: open a hot tap for several minutes with no flame, smoking or other ignition source near it (Bradford White electric, A.O. Smith gas).
Put a clean container under the drain valve at the bottom (or screw on a hose). Open the valve slowly. Plastic drain valves break easily: turn them gently.
Set the first few litres aside: water from a tank can carry particles of iron and other minerals (Alberta emergency water). Let them settle and use them for washing. Collect the rest.

If you are unsure of the water, treat it before drinking. If it is cloudy, clear it first: let it settle and draw off the clear water, or pour it through a clean cloth (CDC make water safe). Then boil it at a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 ft, about 2,000 m), or add unscented household bleach: 2 drops per litre of clear water at 5 to 9 % bleach, double if the water is cloudy or very cold, then let it stand at least 30 minutes (CDC make water safe). Or use [solar disinfection](#guides/skill_solar_disinfection). A filter on its own doesn't remove every germ: disinfect after filtering (CDC make water safe; see [Water filters](#guides/reference_water_filters)).

Find the anode: a large hex head on top of the tank (A.O. Smith's anode takes a 1-1/16 in, about 27 mm, socket), sometimes under a cap and foam (A.O. Smith gas). On some tanks it is built into the hot outlet fitting instead (Bradford White electric).

With the cold inlet closed, a hot tap open and about 19 litres (5 US gal) drained (A.O. Smith gas), undo the anode with a long-handled socket. It is often seized; have a helper hold the tank and use a long lever.
steps.warn: Brace yourself. If the socket slips you can hit pipes or fall. On a gas heater that is still connected, don't let the tank twist or shift on its gas pipe: if the anode won't turn without the tank moving, leave it.

steps.text: Pull the rod straight up. A.O. Smith says its anode can be as long as 89 cm (35 in) (A.O. Smith gas), so allow headroom. If the ceiling is too low, bend it as it comes out or saw it in two.

Check the rod: a heavy coat of magnesium on a steel core wire is good; just the bare wire is spent. Scrape a few shavings and hold a flame to them: magnesium burns with a blinding white flame. Aluminium does not.
steps.warn: Don't look straight at burning magnesium and never use water on it.

steps.text: Electric: with the tank drained, take off the access panels, push the insulation aside, unclip the thermostats and unscrew the heating elements with a large socket.

Gas: take the gas control valve, its thermocouple and the piezo igniter only from a heater that is already disconnected from its gas pipe: at a scrapyard, on the curb, or already taken out. If the heater is still connected, leave its gas side alone: close its own gas valve, set the control to OFF, don't shift the tank on its gas connector, and take only the water and the anode. See [Gas at a damaged house](#guides/safety_natural_gas).
steps.warn: Never undo a gas joint or take a gas valve off a connected line: an open line leaks, and a disconnected line must be capped by someone qualified (see the gas safety card). A heater that has been under water must be replaced (A.O. Smith gas): don't reuse its gas control on gas.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Stored water.** The biggest prize. Tanks vary: A.O. Smith's manual lists 40 and 50 US gallon (about 150 and 190 litre) models, and Bradford White's electric manual covers 19 to 119 US gallons (72 to 450 litres) (A.O. Smith gas, Bradford White electric). At 4 litres a person a day (Alberta emergency water), one 150-litre tank gives a family of four more than a week. CDC lists the tap water heater tank as a clean source (CDC emergency water). A rotten-egg smell is the most common complaint about the anode, and comes from hydrogen sulphide dissolved in the water (A.O. Smith gas). It takes sulphate in the water, little dissolved oxygen, sulphate-reducing bacteria in the tank and extra hydrogen from the anode all at once, and A.O. Smith calls the bacteria harmless to people. Treat the water if in doubt.
- **Magnesium anode.** Shave it with a knife or file into a small pile of fine curls, about the size of a coin, under your tinder. Light the pile with a ferro rod spark or a flame: it burns at a very high temperature, even when damp, and lights stubborn tinder. One rod gives hundreds of fires. Store shavings dry in a sealed tin.
- **Heating elements.** Screw-in elements for mains voltage: the maximum wattage and rated voltage are on the heater's data plate (Bradford White electric), so read the stamp on the flange too. On a lower voltage they make much less heat; on 12 V they are almost useless. Good for diverting surplus solar or generator power into hot water.
- **Thermostats.** Snap-action thermostats with an adjustable setting: good for any heating control.
- **Gas parts.** A standing-pilot gas heater has a thermocouple in the pilot flame, wired to the combination gas valve, and a piezo igniter that sparks at the pilot when pressed (Bradford White service). Take them only from a heater that is already disconnected from its gas pipe (see the last step and [Gas at a damaged house](#guides/safety_natural_gas)).
- **The tank and insulation.** The steel tank holds pressure and makes a good water store or a solar water heater core. Foam insulation from the jacket is useful too.

## Getting water out when you can't drain

If the drain valve is broken or blocked, undo the hot outlet pipe on top and siphon from there with a clean hose.

## Variations

- Some tanks use aluminium or zinc-aluminium anodes, not magnesium. Test shavings before relying on them.
- Tankless heaters store almost no water and have no anode.
- Older homes may also have a tank that supplies hot water to radiators. CDC says to use the tap water heater tank, not the home heating system tank (CDC emergency water).
- Commercial buildings have larger tanks, sometimes several, and boilers with storage cylinders.

## What to leave

- The tank, unless you can move it: even empty it is heavy, so get a second person before you lift it.
- The jacket sheet metal is thin.
